original_test_intent: Verify the installed modules are the approved3DS RDIMM parts with expected rank/stack/type, count, capacity and slots1-24 topology across BIOS and Linux.
original_method: Operator captures BIOS slot map; agent securely collects unfiltered DMI/meminfo/free/NUMA; engineering binds part/serial/type-detail/rank/stack or vendor SPD documentation to3DS identity and reconciles capacity/accounting.
manual_activity: Operator/KVM captures slots1-24; engineering supplies3DS identity authority; agent collects secure Linux evidence.
required_inputs: Exact3DS RDIMM manufacturer/part/serial/type/rank/stack/SPD or vendor-spec identity method
Approved population, capacity, speed, ECC and slot1-24 matrix
Secure Linux DMI/meminfo/free/NUMA plus any approved SPD decoder
Installed-versus-usable accounting, ECC/SEL/thermal abort and recovery policy
safety_requirements: Read-only inspection; no reseat or BIOS change
Preserve populated/empty slots and raw identity fields
Stop on wrong host, ECC/SEL error, unstable boot or missing/contradictory3DS evidence
agent_execution_scope: Collect BIOS-supplied evidence from operator and secure full OS memory records
Map part/rank/stack indicators and accounting to supplied3DS spec
Do not infer3DS from capacity/type alone, perform physical changes or issue verdict

review_improvement: Adds the missing3DS-specific acceptance so generic RDIMM inventory cannot falsely satisfy the variant.
independent_technical_reasoning: 3DS describes stacked DRAM architecture and may not be exposed directly by SMBIOS. A module can have the same capacity as a non-3DS design, so size/count is not identity proof. Approved part/SPD/vendor evidence must be joined to slot and serial data before the testcase's named technology is covered.
